clue.text: Children's entertainer with a weakness for pot?

definitions.text: Children's entertainer with a weakness for pot?

parts.words: Children's entertainer with a weakness for pot?
parts.note: a much-loved storybook bear who entertains children and cannot resist a honey pot; 'pot' slyly suggests cannabis or a pot belly

explanation.surface: A children's party performer with a secret drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' seems to mean cannabis, but the pot is a honey pot, the bear's famous craving in A. A. Milne's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Milne's honey-loving bear has entertained generations of young readers.

clue.text: This will make clearer what you are driving at

definitions.text: This will make clearer what you are driving at

parts.words: This will make clearer what you are driving at
parts.note: 'what you are driving at' reads as your meaning, but literally it is the road ahead as seen through a car's front glass

explanation.surface: A device that clarifies the point you are trying to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What you are driving at' sounds like an argument's point; read literally it is the road you steer towards, kept visible by the blade on the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The motorised blade sweeps rain off a car's front glass so the driver sees the road.

clue.text: In Tauranga I observe such a tree?

indicators.note: 'In' says the letters sit inside the run of words Tauranga I observe

explanation.surface: A traveller in a New Zealand city spots a particular tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across TauraNGA I Observe; Tauranga is a New Zealand city, which is why 'such a tree' fits a native NZ species.
explanation.definitionFit: The ngaio is a small evergreen tree native to New Zealand.

clue.text: Style of drawing — one with a certain amount of optical illusion, for the most part

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a certain amount means some

indicators.note: 'for the most part' says most of the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: an optical illusion is a trick of the eye

explanation.surface: Describing a drawing style that relies largely on visual deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the most part' drops the last letter of TRICK, leaving TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometric projection is a technical drawing method showing three axes at equal angles.

clue.text: Revolutionary unit is overturning a republic in Africa

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests the word unit is turned over and its letters rearranged

parts.note: the four letters of unit as fodder

indicators.note: overturning says the little word is is turned back to front

parts.note: the word is, written backwards

explanation.surface: A rebel military unit topples the government of an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' and 'overturning' both read as politics, a coup toppling a state; one scrambles the first word, the other turns the second back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African state that has been a republic since 1957.

clue.text: Globe theatre reconstructed without wings

indicators.note: reconstructed, like a rebuilt playhouse, says the remaining letters are put together in a new order
a theatre's wings are its sides, so 'without wings' takes off the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Globe playhouse has been rebuilt, minus its side stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without wings' strips T and E from THEATRE, leaving HEATR; 'reconstructed' rearranges that. 'Globe' looks like part of the theatre's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet is often called the globe.

clue.text: Stay in the dark? Nearly in public

indicators.note: 'in' tells us one word sits inside another

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
nigh is an old word for nearly

explanation.surface: Should you keep secret, or almost go public?
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the dark' sounds like ignorance, but the definition means staying through the night, and 'Nearly' is a synonym, not a trimming signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An overnight stay lasts through the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Voltaire accepted none of the terms of this European unification

definitions.text: Voltaire accepted none of the terms of this European unification

parts.words: Voltaire accepted none of the terms of this European unification
parts.note: Voltaire quipped that a certain medieval realm was neither sacred, nor from Rome, nor an imperial power

explanation.surface: The French philosopher rejected the conditions of a European union treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' seems to mean treaty conditions; in fact it is the three words of the realm's name, each of which Voltaire said was false.
explanation.definitionFit: This medieval confederation of central European territories lasted until 1806 under an elected emperor.

clue.text: Old American gets home to California

parts.note: being in means being at home
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A veteran American returns home to the West Coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were a people of ancient Peru, so of old South America.

clue.text: Person with possessions gives debtor new heart

indicators.note: giving the debtor a new 'heart' means putting a letter in the middle of the word

parts.note: a debtor is one who owes, an ower

explanation.surface: A rich man changes his attitude towards someone who owes him.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes into the middle of OWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has possessions possesses them, so holds title to them.

clue.text: Girl turning every Englishman's head

indicators.note: turning says the pieces that follow are read backwards

parts.note: every means all

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl attracts the gaze of every Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL plus E (the head of 'Englishman') gives ALLE, which 'turning' reverses. 'Turning ... head' looks like the girl making men look round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Distress so amused demonic prince

indicators.note: distress suggests the letters are damaged and pulled out of shape

parts.note: fodder of eight letters

explanation.surface: Being so amused upsets a devilish nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress' rearranges SO AMUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Asmodeus is a king of devils in Jewish legend, found in the Book of Tobit.

clue.text: Suspended railway with unsatisfactory 'fare levels?

parts.note: suspended means hung

explanation.surface: A hanging railway that charges poor fares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' is food, not a ticket price: someone whose intake of food is too low is hungry. The apostrophe before 'fare' is a print blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose food intake falls short of need feels empty and ravenous.

clue.text: Old TV series never lacking for direction?

definitions.meaning: a long-running British soap opera (1964-88) set in a Midlands motel
a place where roads meet always offers a choice of ways to go

explanation.walkthrough: Crossroads was a long-running British TV soap opera set in a motel.
explanation.definitionFit: A road junction offers several routes, and the soap took its name from a motel at such a junction.

clue.text: Unit doesn't behave like this at any time during sortie

indicators.note: 'during' places one word within the span of another

parts.note: a sally is a sortie, a sudden rush out
ever means at any time

explanation.surface: A military unit misbehaves at some point on a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: A unit acts as one body, never each member separately, so the definition describes what it does not do.
explanation.definitionFit: Severally means individually or separately, the opposite of acting as a unit.

clue.text: High on drug, a female 'is oblivious to sound

parts.note: stoned means high on drugs
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A woman high on drugs fails to hear anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe before 'is' is a print blemish; the paper reads plain 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone completely unable to hear notices no noise at all.

clue.text: Pass round macs, originally, as protection from rain

indicators.note: 'round' says the first word encircles another letter

parts.note: a gap is a mountain pass

indicators.note: originally means take the first letter

explanation.surface: Raincoats are handed round to keep off the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: M, the first letter of 'macs', goes inside GAP. A gamp is an old British word for a large umbrella, from Mrs Gamp in Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamp is an umbrella, especially a big unwieldy one.

clue.text: Fuel getting very heated on the way back

indicators.note: 'on the way back' says the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: red, as in red-hot, means heated

explanation.surface: A motorist's fuel gets very hot on the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: V plus RED gives VRED, reversed. Derv is the British name for diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is diesel oil used in road vehicles.

clue.text: Inspection arranged in North London

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of inspection are put in a new order

parts.note: fodder of ten letters

explanation.surface: An inspection is set up in a part of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges INSPECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Cispontine means on the near (north) side of London's Thames bridges.

clue.text: Seafood and soy — horseradish in most instances — for starters

definitions.text: Seafood and soy — horseradish in most instances — for starters

indicators.note: 'for starters' takes the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Raw fish with soy sauce and usually horseradish makes a Japanese first course.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of seven words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes the dish, served with soy and wasabi (Japanese horseradish).
explanation.definitionFit: Sashimi is sliced raw fish, eaten with soy sauce and wasabi, often as an appetiser.

clue.text: Without conflict, they offer share options

definitions.text: Without conflict, they offer share options

parts.words: Without conflict, they offer share options
parts.note: in peacetime blades of war may be beaten into ploughshares, as in Isaiah, so they provide a 'share' option

explanation.surface: In peaceful times, companies grant their employees stock options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Share options' sounds like stock-market perks; the share is a ploughshare, which the Bible says weapons will be beaten into when war ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladed weapons of war, in the biblical image, are reforged as ploughshares in peace.

clue.text: Little girl holding record for flower section

indicators.note: 'holding' says the first word contains the second

parts.note: Sal is a short form of Sally or Sarah
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A small girl clutches a record in a florist's department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little girl' gives a pet form of a name, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like parts forming the outer whorl of a flower.

clue.text: Period for broadcasting across the country

definitions.text: Period for broadcasting across the country

parts.words: Period for broadcasting across the country
parts.note: broadcasting means radio or TV transmission nationwide, but literally it is scattering grain by hand over the countryside

explanation.surface: Airtime for a national radio or TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' suggests radio; its original sense is sowing by scattering, and 'the country' is farmland, not the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the season of the year when farmers sow.

clue.text: Underground root, primarily

parts.note: the Tube is London's Underground railway

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A root that lives below the soil, chiefly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the nickname for the London Underground. 'Underground' reads as describing the root, which is also what the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber, such as a potato, is a swollen underground storage stem or root.

clue.text: Work with aluminium and stone

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Working with metal and stone, like a craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone with a play of colours.

clue.text: In speech, peer's outstanding

indicators.note: 'in speech' says the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: to peer is to pry, so a person who peers pries

explanation.surface: A lord's speech is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a nobleman, but it is the verb: someone who peers pries.
explanation.definitionFit: Prize as an adjective means first-rate, worthy of an award, as in a prize specimen.

clue.text: Ship that crosses river up North

definitions.meaning: in Scotland and northern England the dialect word for a bridge, which spans a river

explanation.walkthrough: In northern English and Scottish dialect a bridge is called a brig.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted sailing vessel, and in northern dialect also a bridge over water.

clue.text: Carry aerofoil when flying? It's to be hoped they do!

definitions.text: Carry aerofoil when flying? It's to be hoped they do!

indicators.note: 'when flying' suggests the letters are tossed about in the air

parts.note: fodder of thirteen letters

explanation.surface: Airmen hope their wings keep them aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When flying' rearranges CARRY AEROFOIL, and the whole clue describes British airmen, who must keep wings aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's air arm flies aircraft whose wings are aerofoils.
